questions.q: Why does this capstone use a dedicated new workspace rather than reusing one from an earlier chapter's lab?
options: A dedicated workspace keeps this project's permissions, refresh schedule, and app cleanly separate from unrelated earlier work
Power BI requires a new workspace for every single report
Dedicated workspaces are free while shared ones cost extra
Reusing a workspace is technically impossible
questions.explain: A workspace scoped to just this project avoids mixing its permissions, refresh configuration, and app with unrelated content from earlier labs.

questions.q: What gets published when you select File → Publish → Publish to Power BI from Desktop?
options: Only the visible report pages, never the semantic model
Only the semantic model, with no report pages at all
Only the first page of the report
The semantic model (tables, relationships, measures) and all report pages, including hidden ones like the drillthrough page, as one unit
questions.explain: Publishing sends the entire semantic model plus every report page — visible and hidden (like a drillthrough target) — together as one published unit.

questions.q: What does pinning tiles from the three report pages onto a dashboard accomplish?
options: It permanently deletes the original report pages
It creates a single-page, at-a-glance view where each tile still links back to its full report page for detail
It disables all interactivity on the underlying reports
It automatically shares the dashboard with the entire organization
questions.explain: This directly applies Lesson 74's dashboard concept — tiles pinned from multiple reports give a consolidated glance view, each still linking back to its source report.

questions.q: What are the three tabs used when packaging this capstone into an app?
options: Import, Transform, and Load
Design, Build, and Test
Setup, Content, and Audience
Publish, Share, and Delete
questions.explain: This is the same three-tab app-publishing flow from Lesson 73: Setup names and describes the app, Content adds the report/dashboard, and Audience defines who sees it.

questions.q: Does publishing an app automatically mean the right people can see it and that it will stay current with new data?
options: Publishing only handles refresh, not access
No — sharing specific access and configuring refresh are separate, deliberate steps covered in Lesson 92
Yes, publishing handles both automatically with no further action
Publishing only handles access, not refresh
questions.explain: Publishing the app is not the same as granting access to specific people or setting up a refresh schedule — both remain separate steps that Lesson 92 addresses directly.
